title: rust/lichen-schc/src/context.rs: MSB shift can overflow for 128-bit fields
description:
In rule_matches(), when processing Mo::Msb, the shift amount is computed as `fd.length_bits - mo_arg`. For 128-bit fields (like IPv6 addresses) with mo_arg=0, shift equals 128. The expression `val >> 128` where val is u128 causes a panic in debug mode ('attempt to shift right with overflow') and silently produces 0 in release mode.

Fix suggestion: Use checked_shr or add explicit bounds: if shift >= 128 { return true; /* 0 prefix bits matches anything */ } or reject mo_arg=0 as invalid configuration.

File: rust/lichen-schc/src/context.rs
Line: 187
Category: overflow
close_reason: Fix already implemented at line 246-248: the code checks `if mo_arg == 0 { continue; }` before computing the shift, preventing the 128-bit shift overflow. The comment at lines 241-243 documents this design. Test `msb_matching_handles_full_width_boundaries()` at line 554 explicitly validates this case with length_bits=128 and mo_arg=0.
